name: Ameth'Aran
summary: Broken colonnades rise from Ameth'Aran in southern Darkshore, where restless ghosts haunt the stones. Once a great Highborne city, it fell when the Well of Eternity collapsed and shattered the ancient world.

sections.title: A City of Sorcerers
sections.body: Before the Great Sundering, Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran were twin centers of Highborne influence along the ancient coastline. Queen Azshara favored Ameth'Aran, where its ruling nobles pursued unrestrained arcane experiments. Their sorcerer, Athrikus Narassin, governed from afar in the Tower of Althalaxx. The city flourished until the Well of Eternity collapsed and tore the Kaldorei Empire apart.

sections.title: Betrayal and Eternal Torment
sections.body: As the world began to tear apart, Athrikus Narassin returned to Ameth'Aran and promised salvation through powerful shielding magic. Instead, he stole his subjects' life force to feed his soul gems. He disguised the betrayal as a promise of eternal preservation. Dark magic and a great cataclysm shattered Ameth'Aran, and anguished Highborne specters still stalk its grounds, unable to rest ten thousand years after their murder.

faq.answer: In the Kaldorei Empire's final days, Ameth'Aran already lay in ruins. Then the Well of Eternity shattered during the Great Sundering and destroyed the city ten thousand years ago. The spirits of Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins.

faq.q: Who are the ghosts wandering the ruins?
faq.answer: The ghosts are restless Highborne elves who lived and practiced arcane magic in Ameth'Aran before the Great Sundering. Unable to rest, they wander the broken stones in unending agony and fury.

Anaya Dawnrunner lived in Ameth'Aran and was beloved by Cerellean Whiteclaw. She died when the city fell during the Sundering. Her ghost remained bound to the ruins until Cerellean sought outside aid to release her soul.

faq.q: What are the stone tablets found in the ruins?
faq.answer: The stone tablets bear Ameth'Aran's history and an account of its fall. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade tried to decipher them for a historical report to the Cenarion Circle, but hostile ghosts forced her to rely on passing travelers.

angles.text: As a night elf, you can see Ameth'Aran as a grim monument to the Highborne caste's hubris and treachery, which brought about the Sundering.
As a druid, you can see these ruins as an unhealed scar on Darkshore. Tormented spirits linger here and disrupt the natural balance of the wilds.
